events.title: Birth of the future emperor Hadrian
events.description: Publius Aelius Hadrianus was born into a Roman family with roots in Hispania. He became emperor in 117 AD.
events.significance: Hadrian ruled Rome at its height. He is remembered for consolidating the empire's borders, most famously with Hadrian's Wall in Britain, and for his large building projects.

events.title: Frederick the Great is born
events.description: The future king of Prussia was born in Berlin. He took the throne in 1740 and became one of the best-known monarchs in European history.
events.significance: Frederick turned Prussia into a major European military and political power. He also became a patron of the arts and a leading figure of the Enlightenment.

events.title: Gold is discovered at Sutter's Mill
events.description: James W. Marshall found gold at a sawmill site in Coloma, California. The discovery set off the California Gold Rush, and some 300,000 people eventually made their way to the region.
events.significance: The Gold Rush reshaped the American West. It sped up California's path to statehood and drew people from around the world.

events.title: The Apple Macintosh goes on sale
events.description: Apple began selling the Macintosh, a compact personal computer. It followed a famous Super Bowl commercial that aired two days earlier.
events.significance: The Mac was the first commercially successful personal computer with a graphical interface and a mouse. It helped bring computing to ordinary users.
